Subject: [Redwood] Short advisory: p99 elevation on hosted /v1/generate (us-west) — next steps

Sarah —

Thanks for the report and the sample request IDs. We see the same p99 elevation in our telemetry for USW between ~07:40–09:00 PST. Initial triage indicates a recent kernel rollout combined with a routing split increased tail queuing on a subset of nodes (we're seeing ~3–4% of nodes with elevated per-token compute latency).

Immediate actions we have taken:
- Rolled back the kernel change on affected USW pools (in progress).
- Throttled routing split to route traffic away from the impacted node set.
- Enabled temporary tighter batching limits for long-sequence (>1024 tokens) requests.

Impact and ETA:
- User-visible p99 should begin improving within 20–30 minutes after rollback and routing changes.
- We will leave Status: "Degraded" on the status page until p99 stabilizes for two consecutive 15-min windows.

Attachments: mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook steps and verification checklist), diagnostic_span_logs_20270228.txt (selected spans)

Public status link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/USW-p99-2027-02-28
Ticket: SUP-3247

I will follow up with a short postmortem once we've validated the rollback. Please let us know if you need further details or want a quick join on a call.

Regards,
Ben Carter

Quick internal update —

- Rollback completed at 09:10 PST and routing adjustment enacted. Observed p99 drop beginning at ~09:25 PST and stabilized by 10:00 PST.
- We kept the status page in "Degraded" until three consecutive 15-minute windows of p99 within expected bounds (completed by 16:45 PST). Status page updated to "Operational" at 16:50 PST.
- Root cause: a regressed kernel micro-optimization that increased per-token compute on long sequences when combined with a recent routing split.

Post-incident actions (short list):
1) Gate kernel rollout with additional canary traffic that includes long-sequence requests.
2) Add telemetry alert for sudden p99 step-ups correlated with kernel binary changes.
3) Document rollback verification steps in the runbook and add a one-click routing dampener.

I'll assemble a slim postmortem and send to stakeholders tomorrow. Ben — please close SUP-3247 with the final span traces attached. Mina — please share the postmortem link with AlphaMed when ready.
